newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's TCV raises 96/97 funding estimate.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's TCV raises 96/97 funding estimate.

text.p: The Treasury Corporation of Victoria (TCV) raised its indicative funding programme for the year to June 30, 1997, to A$2.563 billion from an earlier estimate of A$2.100 billion.
This compares with a funding requirement in 1995/96 of A$3.5 billion, which was made up entirely due to refinancing activity, the borrowing arm for Victoria state said.
The original estimate for 1996/97 also entirely consisted of refinancing activity.
The increase "reflects an additional A$463 million net new money requirement following the settlement of the Petroleum Resource Rent Tax issue," TCV said.
TCV said that based on its current liability profile and Victorian budget estimates for 1996/97, its impact on the markets will be an A$800 million repayment.
State government privatisations have generated over A$13 billion in the past 18 months for the purpose of debt retirement, which TCV has managed.
The government has said further privatisations were likely in 1997, and while these would affect TCV's call on markets, the timing and details of further asset sales was not yet known.
The privatisation proceeds were applied to reducing near term maturities and less liquid issues, in line with TCV's commitment to maintaining the liquidity of its hot stocks.

TCV said while it remained committed to Australia's inflation indexed bond market, given the recent reduction in Victorian debt levels, "TCV has examined options to reduce indexed exposure in line with general reduction of TCV's balance sheet."
